ai.title: Switch to expansion diff strategy for file changes
ai.summary: Backend now generates unified patches via `generatePatch` instead of search/replace blocks, updating `FileChanges` type to string array in `common/src/actions.ts`. `npm-app` applies these using `diff` library's `applyPatch` in `project-files.ts`, replacing manual string replacement logic. `system-prompt.ts` instructs model to use terminal commands for file deletion/renaming, removing `[DELETE]` token support. `knowledge.md` documents the new strategy and client-side application flow.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to edit files, it now describes changes as precise patches (like a recipe of exact line changes) instead of replacing whole blocks of text, which makes edits more reliable and especially helps with large or complex files. The assistant no longer uses a special token to delete files and instead runs terminal commands, so deleting or renaming files is now done through standard commands. You won't see these changes directly in your code, but behind the scenes the system now tracks exactly what to add, remove, or modify line by line, reducing the chance of messy or incorrect edits. These updates are live today in Manicode's editing workflow.

ai.title: Fix patch file path extraction in applyChanges
ai.summary: getFilePathFromPatch now parses 'Index: <path>' headers instead of 'diff --git' lines. applyChanges uses this helper to resolve file paths and passes the full patch string to applyPatch, replacing manual line splitting. Covers common/src/util/file.ts and npm-app/src/project-files.ts. Ensures compatibility with patch formats using standard Index headers.

eli5.text: You may have noticed that applying project changes from a patch file sometimes failed, even when the file path was clearly listed. The software now reads the file path from a standard 'Index:' header line instead of guessing from a different format, and it passes the whole patch through at once instead of chopping it up manually. This makes the tool more reliably apply changes you send it, so you no longer get silent errors just because a patch used a slightly different layout.

ai.title: System prompt: stop re-reading files already in context
ai.summary: backend/src/system-prompt.ts instructs the agent not to call update_file_context for files already included in the <relevant_files> block. Redundant read loops caused the agent to request files it already had, wasting tokens and blocking edits. musings.knowledge.md logs the observed loop where the agent greps for changes that never landed because it kept re-fetching the same file.

eli5.text: When the assistant is working on a task, it gets handed a set of relevant files to read up front. Before this change, it kept asking to read those same files over and over, not realizing it already had them, which wasted time and tokens. The instruction given to the assistant now tells it explicitly not to re-request those files, and the notes file recorded the looping behavior that prompted this fix. You wouldn’t see anything new or different in how the assistant behaves on your end, but it should no longer spin its wheels re-reading the same material.

ai.title: JSON stringify message history in request files prompt
ai.summary: Message content in request files prompt is now JSON stringified. This ensures proper escaping and serialization of user and assistant messages within XML tags. Added console logs for file creation and patch generation in main-prompt. Internal change affecting backend prompt construction logic.

eli5.text: When the assistant prepares prompts about your files, it now wraps the conversation history in a protective JSON format before placing it inside the XML tags. This ensures that complex messages (including those with special characters like quotes or newlines) are properly escaped and won't break or confuse the prompt structure. You would notice this if you looked at the prompt files the assistant generates internally, where user and assistant messages now appear with JSON-style string formatting. The change is live today in the backend prompt construction logic.

ai.title: Factor out inner prompt for request files
ai.summary: Refactored `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts` to extract `innerPromptContent` from `generateComprehensiveRequestFilesPrompt`. This isolates message history and file context string generation, applying `STOP_MARKER` stripping via `common/constants`. Internal backend refactor; no user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the system's helper agent got a bit of a spring cleaning. The part of the instructions that tell it how to look at your project files was split into a smaller, more focused piece. This makes it easier to keep track of how it's reading file history and stripping out a special stop marker. If you looked at the actual behavior, nothing would look different, it's just organizing how it thinks before it answers you. It's the kind of change that makes future bug fixes or new tricks easier to add, but doesn't change what you see today.

ai.title: Add action schema diff regression tests
ai.summary: New diff regression tests for `generateDiffs` and `generatePatch` cover `CLIENT_ACTIONS`/`SERVER_ACTIONS` zod schemas in `src/action.ts`. Mock fixtures (`expected.ts`, `new.ts`, `old.ts`) under `backend/src/__tests__/__mock-data__/actions` validate expansion of 3 comment markers. Scope limited to backend test suite; no runtime or model changes.

eli5.text: The team added new automated checks that compare two versions of how the system communicates with itself about things like user messages and file operations, making sure the expanded version still includes all three special comment markers it should. These checks use three sample files (old, new, and expected) placed under backend/src/__tests__/__mock-data__/actions to test both diff and patch generation functions in the backend test suite. If it looks like nothing happens for you right now, that's right because the change is live only within the development team's testing environment; no runtime behavior or features you see are altered by this one.

ai.title: Thread userInputId through WebSocket actions
ai.summary: A required userInputId string is threaded through user-input, response-chunk, response-complete, tool-call, and terminal-command-result actions. The backend forwards it on every sendAction, while the client reuses it for tool-call follow-ups and ignores mismatched response chunks or completion events. The change spans common/src/actions.ts, backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts, npm-app/src/client.ts, npm-app/src/cli.ts, npm-app/package.json, and npm-app/knowledge.md. CLI inputs generate an ID with Math.random().toString(36), and the package adds nanoid plus docs for the client-side correlation system.

eli5.text: Each time you type a message to the assistant, the app now gives that message a unique tracking tag. The backend sends every piece of its reply, text chunks, tool actions, and completion notices, stamped with that same tag, and your device ignores any reply fragments that arrive with the wrong tag. This makes rapid back-to-back questions stop mixing their answers together. The change went live today for everyone using the WebSocket connection, so the next time you send a message while an older reply is still streaming, you simply won't see the stale pieces anymore.
